question: On what Text-Based Games are experiments performed?

evidence: CoinCollector BIBREF8 is a class of text-based games where the objective is to find and collect a coin from a specific location in a given set of connected rooms . The agent wins the game after it collects the coin, at which point (for the first and only time) a reward of +1 is received by the agent. The environment parses only five admissible commands (go north, go east, go south, go west, and take coin) made by two worlds;

CookingWorld BIBREF14 in this challenge, there are 4,440 games with 222 different levels of difficulty, with 20 games per level of difficulty, each with different entities and maps. The goal of each game is to cook and eat food from a given recipe, which includes the task of collecting ingredients (e.g. tomato, potato, etc.), objects (e.g. knife), and processing them according to the recipe (e.g. cook potato, slice tomato, etc.). The parser of each game accepts 18 verbs and 51 entities with a predefined grammar, but the overall size of the vocabulary of the observations is 20,000. In Appendix SECREF36 we provide more details about the levels and the games' grammar.

title: Exploration Based Language Learning for Text-Based Games
answer_rationale: The experiments are performed on CoinCollector and CookingWorld games, as explicitly stated in the retrieved documents. Text 3 mentions these two environments as selected for experiments, with CoinCollector used for benchmarking exploration capabilities and CookingWorld for evaluating generalization capabilities. Text 2 also references text-based computer games in general, but the specific games mentioned in the experiments are CoinCollector and CookingWorld.
